correctness.summary: The proof combines the exact published formula for i(C^2(H)) with a new elementary identity alpha(C(G))=|E(G)| for connected graphs of order at least 3. Substitution gives an exact cancellation and yields i(C^k(G))=2|E(C^{k-2}(G))| for every k>=3. Boundary cases in the independence lemma were checked explicitly, and finite graph-atlas computations agree with the formulas.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The complete accessible text of arXiv:2609.16357v1 was inspected. Its final result is a formula for i(C^2(G)); it contains no C^3 or higher-iterate statement. Exact and synonymous searches for iterated central graphs, third central graphs, C^3(G), C^k(G), and the independence number of central graphs found no equivalent or stronger higher-iterate law. Related work on ordinary domination of central graphs concerns a different parameter.

value.summary: The source formula for the second iterate depends on alpha(G), but from the third iterate onward the independent domination number loses all dependence on the structure of G beyond its order and size. The theorem gives a closed recurrence for every higher iterate and identifies the mechanism through alpha(C(G))=|E(G)|.

limitations: The theorem is stated for finite connected simple graphs of order at least 3.
The proof uses the published same-setting formula for i(C^2(H)).
Finite computation is supporting evidence and does not replace the proof.
Very recent or unindexed parallel work, or older work using different terminology for repeated central-graph operations, may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.
